newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to spend $1 bln on refineries before 2000.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to spend $1 bln on refineries before 2000.

text.p: Colombia will spend more than $1 billion on upgrading the country's two main oil refineries between now and the the year 2000, the state oil company Ecopetrol said Wednesday.

The investment is part of a plan launched in 1995 to boost the efficiency and productivity levels of the plants at the oil- production center of Barrancabermeja, in central Colombia, and in Cartagena, on the Caribbean coast.

"The modernization of the state refineries will increase their efficiency and output to international levels and guarantee Colombian consumers a supply of derivatives (oil products) that are produced in accordance with strict environmental norms," an Ecopetrol statement said.
More than $270 million of the total budget will be spent specifically on environmental controls and plant safety.
Throughput at the Barrancabermeja refinery averaged almost 197,000 barrels per day (bpd) and more than 75,000 bpd at the Cartagena facility.
